question.problem:
What is the solution to the following system of inequalities?

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y-5\le 2 \\ 2y+7>11\end{aligned}
$$

The solution is
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}
$y\le $
{{field-3}}.
question.worked_solution:
To solve the system, we need to find the values of $y$ that satisfy both $y-5\le 2$ and $2y+7>11$ simultaneously.

- First, we solve $y-5\le 2\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-5 & \le 2 \\ y-5+5 & \le 2+5 \\ y & \le 7\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249179/assets/b0107bec7ccb2c56036de405a29870e8cfcc166cc6405f425fc3296ec8f1be2b.png)

$$

$$

- Then, we solve $2y+7>11\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2y+7 & >11 \\ 2y+7-7 & >11-7 \\ 2y & >4 \\ \frac{2y}{2} & >\frac{4}{2} \\ y & >2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249179/assets/59523e51144ef776295ec43032def1bc0192351deb6294fbb2d56acd87bb2cac.png)

$$

$$

To find the values of $y$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249179/assets/981477f5336b96998b61b7ab18647609cb33c12984c14049621ac15c698c25a5.png)

 

$$

$$

Thus, the final solution is $2<y\le 7.$
